factProposals.value: Vendors submit, per requirement, a compliance answer (complies, partially_complies, does_not_comply), a technical approach and up to five PDF, Word or plain-text documents.
A city reviewer approves each vendor submission or requests changes with a comment; a reviewer cannot review their own organisation's submission; an approved requirement accepts no further revisions.
Vendors (scope vendor:submit) and city reviewers (scope vendor:review) appear as API clients in the audit trail.

vendor_submissions (one row per revision, with a SHA-256 fingerprint) and vendor_documents (exact bytes plus fingerprint) exist. The 18 requirements vendors answer are held in server/vendor/requirements.json.
Vendors see only their own submissions and documents; uploaded files must really be the declared type and are only ever downloaded as attachments under a sandboxing policy.
Each vendor gets a compliance status for every requirement (approved, waiting_for_review, changes_requested, not_answered), and reviewers get a queue of waiting submissions with overdue flags.

The STORY-012 brief says to reuse an existing schema and that it is the last story in the plan; no schema existed (built from the proposed compliance_response table) and six stories (STORY-005 to 010) remain. The published plan has no requirements, so the catalog was copied from the STORY-000 brief.
The city's review deadline for vendor submissions, and who the reviewers are, are not known; 5 days is a placeholder.

decisions.statement: Confirm a submission is stored by reading it back and checking its fingerprint inside the transaction before returning a receipt.
decisions.rationale: A vendor must never be told a submission was received when it was not stored exactly as sent.
decisions.evidence: server/vendorSubmissions.js; tests/vendorSubmissions.test.js (does not match what was sent)

decisions.statement: Audit every vendor submission received, including repeats and refusals that store nothing.
decisions.rationale: The Trust criterion covers any submission when it is received, not only stored ones.

decisions.statement: Recognise documents by their content, not their name, and serve them only as downloads.
decisions.rationale: Prevents disguised executables and stops an uploaded file running in a browser.

decisions.statement: Keep a requirements catalog file, checked by a test against the plan's stories, rather than editing plan.json.
decisions.rationale: The published plan has no requirements, and editing plan.json would stop the platform refreshing it.

decisions.statement: Show another vendor's submission as not found.
decisions.rationale: Vendors competing for the same contract must not be able to see or probe each other's answers.

limitations.statement: The portal is API endpoints only; there is no web page for vendors or reviewers yet.
Documents are stored in the database; there is no virus scanning.
Reviewer and vendor identities are API clients, not individual people; per-person logins come with STORY-007.
Nothing notifies a vendor when a review is made, or a reviewer when an item becomes overdue.
